Eurovision Games — every game in the suite

Eurovision Games is the free, browser-based companion for the Eurovision Song Contest. Predictions that lock when voting opens, quiz rounds and head-to-head duels before and during the show, a live dashboard, and five trophies at the end. Two to twenty players, no install, no account for guests.

What's inside Eurovision Games

Four scoring modes layer across the four hours of the broadcast — each one targeting a different beat of the night so that the room never has "nothing to do." Predictions are the long game. Quiz is the warm-up. Duels are the live-show weapon. The Dashboard is the running scoreboard everyone is watching.

GameWhen activeScoring (cap)
PredictionsParty start → lock when voting opensTop 5 + Worst 5, 50 exact / 20 in list, 500 cap
QuizParty start → lock when voting opens3 rounds × 120 = 360 cap
DuelsParty start → lock when voting opens3 questions, 12s each, Steal or Double
DashboardAlwaysLive total of all four sources

Predictions — Top 5 and Worst 5

Before or during the show, every player builds a Top 5 and a Worst 5 from the 2026 grand-final running order, and can keep editing until voting opens. An exact position pays 50 points and the right list at the wrong rank pays 20; the formula scores against the official jury + televote total as soon as the official results come in. The hard cap is 500 points so no single category can run the night.

Full format on the predictions game page.

Quiz rounds

Each player plays three rounds at their own pace: ten questions each, fifteen seconds per question, drawn from the same Eurovision trivia bank that feeds duels. Quiz opens when the host starts the party and locks automatically when voting opens — that is the cutoff. Cap is 360 across all three rounds combined.

Sample questions and the bank breakdown live on the Eurovision trivia page.

Duels

Duels open as soon as the host starts the party and run alongside the quiz until voting opens. A duel is a private 3-question, 12-second-per-question head-to-head with another player. There is no win bonus — the winner picks Steal (move their duel score from the loser) or Double (add twice their duel score to themselves). Two trophies — Duelist and Thief — are decided here.

Full rules and scoring on the duels page.

Live Dashboard

The Dashboard is the always-visible leaderboard, push-updated the moment any of the four sources resolves — predictions, quiz, duels won, points stolen. Tap a player for their per-source split. There is no refresh and no spectator mode; everyone in the room sees the same totals at the same time.

Deep dive on the Dashboard page.

Trophies — five winners every night

Eurovision Games does not crown one winner — it crowns five. After the official Eurovision result is entered, trophy cards reveal one by one:

  • Champion — highest total across all four sources.
  • Oracle — best prediction score (Top 5 + Worst 5 combined).
  • Guru — most correct quiz answers across the three rounds.
  • Duelist — most duels won across the night.
  • Thief — most points taken via Steal.

Free, no install, no account

Eurovision Games is free to play and built to remove every reason a guest might bail before the first song.

  • Browser-based. Any modern browser on iOS, Android, or desktop.
  • Mobile-first PWA. Add to home screen if you want, but you do not have to.
  • No signup at all. The host just creates the room; guests type a room code and a display name.
  • 2–20 players. Sweet spot is 6–10 — enough variety without the trivia rotation getting stale.
